cim: $2 trillion wiped from tech stocks amid artificial intelligence spending fears
cim_eredeti: $2 trillion wiped from tech stocks amid artificial intelligence spending fears
szoveg_eredeti:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 is set to erase more than $2 trillion in market value this month, as Big Tech earnings intensify investor scrutiny over whether massive investments in artificial intelligence can yield returns quickly enough.

The market wipeout slightly exceeds the total valuation of SpaceX. The index has dropped over 5.8% so far in October as the AI trade hit turbulence, with hyperscalers Meta Platforms, Alphabet, and Amazon.com raising their capital expenditure forecasts to accelerate the expansion of their AI infrastructure.

The prospect of mounting AI spending has unnerved investors, particularly as rising borrowing costs make debt-financed investments more expensive and harder to justify.

The downturn accompanies a wave of megacap quarterly reports, with Apple set to release earnings next week and AI industry bellwether Nvidia scheduled for mid-November.

Alphabet experienced its largest single-day percentage decline on record on Thursday following disappointing results in its primary search advertising business and a significant acceleration in cash burn.

Meanwhile, Meta’s plan for a record $97.5 billion fundraise heightened concerns regarding shareholder dilution and whether Big Tech firms will increasingly rely on capital markets.

Microsoft and SpaceX broke from the overall gloom, posting results that demonstrated AI investments are beginning to pay off.

"It may be that we've overestimated how strong the growth might be, but they're not going negative in aggregate," said John Bilton, global head of strategic research at Multi-Asset Solutions.

"We have an insatiable and growing demand for data."

Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise roughly $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years.

Other hyperscalers, including Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet, have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in corporate bonds over the past four years, raising concerns among investors about overreliance on debt financing.

Morgan Stanley projects that total capital expenditure on AI infrastructure will cross $1 trillion next year.

The growing reliance of AI companies on debt capital is surfacing as a fresh risk for investors, challenging the assumption that the firms driving the AI boom are shielded from broader macroeconomic pressures.

The anxiety is moving into credit markets, where investors are pricing in the risk that elevated financing costs and delayed returns could strain corporate balance sheets.

Still, revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has stayed resilient since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, demonstrating strong market demand.

Amazon’s cloud unit, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, Meta posted higher-than-expected revenue growth alongside a positive outlook, and Microsoft projected strong expansion in its cloud business.

However, capital expenditure has reached historic levels. J.P. Morgan forecasts global AI capex will reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, with $900 billion spent in 2026 alone.

Analysts at the firm noted that combined AI spend this year by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, and Microsoft will likely equal their cumulative investment since ChatGPT was introduced in November 2022.
